evaluated_proposal.name: Execute the currently discovered unique GNU ld argv directly
evaluated_proposal.intended_saving: With an established direct-link execution contract, clang becomes a fresh argv producer rather than final execution dependency. Its physical identity and ldd closure could then be omitted from the direct result key, while actual linker/tool deps, environment, full inputs, search negatives and pre/post discovery remain. evaluated_proposal.nearest_counterexample: A custom --clang wrapper can delegate -### to genuine clang yet inject an error, additional input, environment or post-link transformation in its real invocation. Executing the printed ld command bypasses that required behavior. A shell-wrapper rejection is insufficient: an ELF wrapper has the same counterexample. Neither ELF magic nor clang-looking version/output establishes semantic driver authority.
evaluated_proposal.blocked_proof: No existing supported-driver capability/receipt proves this configured driver is replaceable by its printed job without rehashing its executable or imposing a new contract. Simply deleting clang identity/execution because the command parser accepted its output changes the existing interface.
evaluated_proposal.root_coordination: Root agreed this is unclosed; backend_pipeline confirmed no source edits yet. Reviewer explicitly instructed no implementation/build/merge. No new flag or prototype is needed for this checkpoint.
evaluated_proposal.future_separate_contract_only: An explicit default-off direct-link contract could deliberately define --clang as discovery only, but that is a separately authorized semantic contract and cannot count as a same-contract baseline performance win. If ever pursued, execution admission also needs exactly one output, exact object multiplicity/order, exact actual argv0/cwd/environment, no hidden response/multiple jobs, and pre/post fresh binding. The old key parser must not automatically be promoted into execution authority.
evaluated_proposal.disposition: REJECTED by custom-driver wrapper counterexample under the current contract, not merely deferred optimization. The first282MB clang content hash remains necessary to its current installed-tool identity contract because there is no GNU build ID and no prior complete identity.
